interpretation: Focal Thalassia persistence history retains positive recovery information after generic continuous seagrass-habitat history, stable transect identity, loss-year vegetation state, source mixed-species state and loss year are represented. This supports a focal-specific local legacy signal beyond generic vegetated-microsite history.
ecological_boundary: The supported focal-specific history signal still does not identify clonal memory or residual rhizomes. The bare-loss subgroup null and unresolved history-by-continuity interaction imply that focal history is informative but not a simple autonomous below-ground carryover mechanism.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc history decomposition on an already-opened recovery endpoint.
Do not equate the focal-specific coefficient with direct evidence of clonal integration, residual rhizomes, or genet survival.
Generic habitat headstart is not supported as an independent recovery predictor under the joint model.
The bare-loss subgroup null remains an important boundary: focal history does not robustly predict return after complete seagrass loss.
Return is recorded reappearance at the same meter mark, not genet-level recolonization.
